text: Banko Liwanag here. Your hospital refund of {amount} is ready. To receive it, first send a small processing fee to {wallet}.
A refund never needs a fee first. Check with the bank through the number on your card.
Banko Liwanag customer care. You asked about a replacement ATM card. We never ask for your PIN or OTP. Please visit a branch to continue.
Real banks never ask for your PIN or OTP. They send you to a branch or to the number on your card.
Banko Liwanag reminder: your loan payment is due on Friday. Please pay at a branch or in our official app. We will not ask for your PIN.
A real reminder sends you to the branch or the official app and never asks for your PIN.
Calls and voice notes come in as transcripts. Some are real, and some are AI voice clones. Read, check, then decide.
Tap or click a check to make it (or use the arrow keys, then Space or Enter): the family secret question, a call back to the saved number, ask another relative, or the official hotline.
Then choose HELP THEM or HANG UP + REPORT. Helping a scam, or hanging up on a real emergency, costs a heart. You have 3 hearts.
A decision backed by proof scores 100 points, plus up to 60 for using few checks. Verified calls in a row raise your multiplier up to x2. A guess without proof scores only 20.
Some checks cannot settle a call (the phone rings out, the line is busy). Try another one. Later calls leave fewer checks that settle it.
Ring ring! Who is this?
A call comes in: "It is me, I am in the hospital, send money now!" Is it really your family? Your job at the switchboard is to find out.
AI can copy a voice
A scammer needs only a short clip to make an AI copy of a voice. It can sound just like your mother, your doctor or your bank.
Tap a check to verify the caller: secret question, call back, ask a relative, or the hotline. Then help them or hang up and report.
Hurry is the red flag
Scammers fake hospital emergencies to rush you. Real emergencies can wait two minutes for a check.
Trust a call after you verify it through a number or a person you already know.
When should I trust it? After I verify the call through a number or a person I already know, never the voice alone.
CONTENT_GUIDE safe facts: free offers that ask for ID numbers, OTPs or health data are a data risk; Data Privacy Act (RA 10173) data minimisation
LUCKY DRAW
FULL NAME?
a lucky draw that asks for your full name
your full name
A name alone looks harmless, but scammers combine it with other bits to sound like someone you know.
FREE LOAD!
BIRTHDAY?
free load that asks for your birthday
your birthday
Your birthday is a common password and ID check, so it helps someone pretend to be you.
FREE APP
CONTACTS?
a free app that asks to read your contacts
your contact list
Your contacts are other people's data too. Scammers use them to message your family and friends.
WIN PHONE!
ID PHOTO?
a phone giveaway that asks for a photo of your ID
a photo of your ID
A photo of your ID can be used to open accounts or take loans in your name.
RAFFLE
PHILHEALTH
a raffle that asks for your PhilHealth number
your PhilHealth number
Your PhilHealth number links to your health records and claims. Scammers want it more than free load.
A real freebie does not ask for your ID, birthday, contacts or PhilHealth number.
Share the least you can. If an offer asks for more than it needs, skip it.
Your health records are valuable. Give them only to your health worker or the official health center.

a health center flyer

APP BADGE
a verified app badge
Press Space, tap or click to jump over puddles, chickens and potholes.
Press the up and down arrows (or W and S), or swipe up and down, to change lane.
Safe freebies (water, clinic flyers, verified badges) ask for nothing and refill your Privacy Shield.
Data traps ask for your birthday, ID photo, PhilHealth number or contacts. Steer around them or jump over them.
The run ends when the Privacy Shield hits 0. You run faster the longer you last.
Wow, freebies everywhere!
Free load, free phones, free everything! Come, run through the barangay with me.
Some "free" things cost your data
Grab the freebies that ask for nothing. Dodge the ones that ask for your details.
Space or tap to jump. Up and down (or swipe) to change lane. Keep your Privacy Shield above zero.
Your PhilHealth number and health records are valuable. Scammers want them more than you want free load.
Trust offers that don't ask for more than they need.
When should I trust it? When an offer doesn't ask for more of my data than it needs.

Help Lola cross the street to the health center. An AI guide says GO or WAIT for the next lane. It is usually right, and sometimes confidently wrong.
Step forward with the GO tile, the Up arrow or W, or tap above Lola. Wait with WAIT, Space or Enter, or tap Lola. Move sideways with the Left and Right arrows or A and D. Down steps back.
Use your own eyes on the traffic. If a vehicle is about to reach Lola, the horn beeps, Lola steps back to the last grass and you lose a heart. You have 3 hearts.

The Trust Meter goes up when you follow the guide and it was right, and when you override it and it was wrong. It goes down when you follow a wrong call or ignore a right one. A higher meter gives a higher score multiplier, up to x2.
Standing still for a moment in front of a road counts as choosing to wait. Each new lane scores 10 points and each trip to the health center 100. The next street is busier.
Come on, Lola, to the health center!
Lola needs to cross a busy street to reach the health center. You will guide her, with a little help from an AI voice.
The AI guide is helpful but not perfect
The guide says GO or WAIT for each lane, and it is usually right. Sometimes it is sure and wrong, and it sounds the same either way.
Tap GO or WAIT, or use the arrow keys. Watch the traffic yourself. The Trust Meter rises when you follow a right call and when you catch a wrong one.
Your eyes count
Health apps help, but your eyes and your health worker know your situation. Do not let a confident voice do all your looking.
Trust the app when it matches what you see. Speak up, and check, when it does not.
When should I trust it? When the app matches what I see. When it does not, I stop and check with a person.

Alarm at six
The alarm rings. Lola Nena has already cooked garlic rice and egg.
Get up and eat breakfast with Lola
A calm breakfast with family is a good start. Mood and friendships both grow a little.
Eat while you go over your notes
A quick review helps you study, but you were quiet at the table.
Sleep twenty more minutes
Rest is real health. But rushing out the door costs you some study time.
The walk to school
Joy waits at the gate. The road to school takes ten minutes.
Walk together and chat
Talking in person with a friend lifts the mood. Friends notice how you really are.
Walk alone and listen to a lesson recording
Good for study. Your friend wished you had talked a little.
Skip breakfast, run, and sleep on the jeepney
A short nap helps, but you started the day hungry and rushed.
Group project
Bea, Joy and Miguel must finish a poster about handwashing by Friday.
Share the work and finish it together
Teamwork spreads the load. You learn and you grow closer.
Do it all yourself so it is done right
You studied a lot, but you are tired and left your teammates out.
Let the others do it
Easy now, but you learned nothing and your teammates are annoyed.
Help from a chatbot
Bea has to write about why vaccines are checked for safety. The class chatbot app is open.
Ask it to explain the idea, then write it in your own words
This is healthy chatbot use: a tool for a task. You learned, and you still check the facts with your teacher or the DOH page.
Ask it to write the whole essay and copy it
You skipped learning, and chatbots can sound sure while being wrong. Your teacher can tell.
Ask your teacher or a classmate for help
People can explain with care and notice when you are stuck.
Homework time
Three subjects of homework are waiting on the table.
Do the hardest one now, with the phone in another room
A hard task is easier with fewer distractions.
Study with Joy at her house
Studying with a friend gets work done and keeps you close.
Nap for an hour first
Rest helps, but homework is still waiting for you.
Joy’s invite
Joy calls from the street: "Volleyball by the barangay court. Come!"
Go and play
Moving and laughing with friends is good for mood and for friendships.
Say no, you have homework
